claims.claim: California limits collection proceedings by debt buyers.
claims.quote: A debt buyer shall not bring suit or initiate an arbitration or other legal proceeding to collect a consumer debt if the applicable statute of limitations on the debt buyer’s claim has expired.
claims.note: The restriction applies to consumer debt and turns on expiration of the limitations period.

claims.claim: Section 1788.56 is part of the Fair Debt Buying Practices Act.
claims.note: The excerpt gives the section number but not the Act’s title.

claims.claim: A debt buyer may not bring a lawsuit to collect a consumer debt once the applicable time limit for suing has run out.
claims.quote: A debt buyer shall not bring suit or initiate an arbitration or other legal proceeding to collect a consumer debt if the applicable statute of limitations on the debt buyer’s claim has expired.
claims.note: The time limit is the one applicable to the debt buyer’s claim.

claims.claim: The same prohibition covers starting an arbitration.
claims.quote: or initiate an arbitration or other legal proceeding to collect a consumer debt if the applicable statute of limitations on the debt buyer’s claim has expired.

claims.claim: The same prohibition covers starting another legal proceeding.
claims.quote: or initiate an arbitration or other legal proceeding to collect a consumer debt if the applicable statute of limitations on the debt buyer’s claim has expired.
claims.note: Other legal proceedings are expressly included.

claims.claim: If sued over an old debt, raise that with the court.
claims.note: The section regulates the debt buyer’s conduct; it gives no instruction to a defendant.

claims.claim: If sued over an old debt, get help.
claims.note: The section does not address seeking help.

claims.claim: An original creditor suing is a different analysis.
claims.quote: A debt buyer shall not bring suit
claims.note: The rule is addressed to debt buyers; the excerpt does not explain what governs an original creditor.

flags.text: The provided text does not verify the Act’s title or supply an original-creditor rule.
The final sentence uses “old debt” as its trigger. Age alone does not establish that the applicable limitations period has expired.
“Raise that with the court and get help” directs the defendant to act without procedural support in the cited section.

result.summary: The excerpt supports the prohibition on debt buyers starting suits, arbitrations, or other legal proceedings after the applicable limitations period expires. It does not establish how a defendant should respond.
